summary: Recorded the project's foundational architecture decision (pure Three.js 3D view, no MapLibre), plus two reusable conventions surfaced from the documentation pass: keep math modules (projection/extrude/osmToScene) erasable-syntax-only so `npm run verify` can run them via Node type stripping, and keep the generation progress bar asymptotic (cap 99%, hit 100% only on first render). Also added YAML frontmatter to architecture/file-tree.md (type: Artifact) to fix E1/E3 OKF conformance and shortened the initial decision slug to resolve W2.

user: Switch the 3D view between Top, Iso, Low, High, and Side camera angles, plus rotate/tilt nudges
what: The 3D viewport now opens in a Top (2D, straight-down) view and offers five camera presets (Top, Iso, Low, High, Side) that fly between positions, with rotate and tilt nudge buttons and a Reset, all over the 3D pane.
why: Gives users deliberate control over viewing angle without manual orbit-dragging, and a clear default top-down orientation.
next: Try the preset and nudge buttons over the 3D pane after generating a map.

claim, add a 4th Persist & inspect stage, and refresh the source layout (measure.ts, view.ts, server/db.ts, InfoDrawer.svelte, routes/api). Refreshed the stale architecture/file-tree.md source entries to match.

summary: Recorded a rule (per-object 3D highlight must be Three.js, not CSS — the WebGL canvas is a single DOM node) and an Entity page for the new standalone /map/[mapId] SSR route + the readMapScene SQLite loader that reconstructs SceneData from saved rows.

Recorded decision: freeform area selection resolves to a bbox Overpass query + client-side point-in-polygon filter that keeps whole objects (clip.ts). Updated overview — intro line, Select stage (▢/✎ toggle + Area type + wikilink to the decision), and domain-module list (added clip.ts) — so the wiki reflects the new selection capability.

user: Draw a freehand shape on the map, not just a rectangle
what: Added a ▢ Rectangle / ✎ Freeform toggle to the 2D selection map. Freeform traces a polygon by click-dragging; generation fetches only the shape's area (bbox query + client-side point-in-polygon filter).
why: Lets you carve out an L-shape, curved edge, or irregular footprint instead of being limited to a rectangular box.
next: Tap the ✎ Freeform button on the selection map and trace an area.

user: Keep using the 3D map while the info drawer is open
what: Removed the full-screen backdrop that swallowed clicks, so you can orbit and click the 3D map while the object drawer stays open on the right.
why: Previously opening the inspector blocked all map interaction; now inspection and exploration happen together.
next: Click an object, then orbit the camera while reading its details.

user: Pan with left mouse, orbit with right mouse
what: Swapped OrbitControls buttons: left now pans, right orbits/rotates (was the reverse). Click-to-select stays on the left button only, so right-drag to orbit never triggers a selection.
why: Matches the preferred control scheme and stops orbit-drag from accidentally selecting objects.
next: Left-drag to pan, right-drag to orbit in the 3D view.

user: Zoom in ~10× closer on the 3D map — right up to individual buildings
what: Lowered the OrbitControls zoom-in floor from 10% of the scene diagonal to 1% (with a 1m absolute floor), so the mouse wheel can bring you much nearer to the buildings instead of stopping far out.
why: On a typical 1km map the old limit kept you ≥100m away, making it hard to inspect individual structures; the new limit lets you get close enough to see building detail. Zoom-out limit and near clip plane are unchanged and remain safe.
next: Open any generated 3D map and scroll to zoom in close on a building (left-drag pans, right-drag orbits).
